title: DNA Extraction Using Qiagen BioSprint® 96 Workstation
author: Lauren Rodriguez

steps.title: Label 2 mL tubes
steps.instruction: Label a 2 mL tube for each sample, including the negative control.

steps.title: Prepare filter housing
steps.instruction: Remove the filter housing from its plastic bag, ensuring the yellow half of the filter faces the bottom; hold the filter upright in an Erlenmeyer flask while opening.

steps.title: Insert filter paper
steps.instruction: Using flame‑sterilized forceps (three passes) and scissors, fold the top filter paper from each sample into a triangle and place it into the corresponding 2 mL tube with the tip at the bottom.

steps.title: Add lysis buffer mixture
steps.instruction: Prepare a mixture of 380 µL TES buffer and 20 µL Proteinase K (total 400 µL) for each sample, adding extra volume for a negative control and pipetting error (≈300 µL per tube is sufficient); pipette the mixture into each tube to fully saturate the filter.

steps.title: Vortex filter tubes
steps.instruction: Vortex the tubes briefly or turn them upside down several times to mix.

steps.title: Incubate lysate
steps.instruction: Incubate all 2 mL tubes at 56 °C for 3 hours (03:00:00).

steps.title: Spin down lysate
steps.instruction: Remove tubes from the incubator and briefly centrifuge to collect the lysate at the tube bottom.

steps.title: Transfer filter to inlet
steps.instruction: Place each filter into a plastic inlet, then return the inlet‑filter assembly to its original 2 mL tube; remove the silica membrane from the inlet.

steps.title: Centrifuge with lid open
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the open‑lid tubes at 14 000 rpm for 10 minutes (temperature not specified).

steps.title: Discard filters
steps.instruction: Throw away the filter pieces; the lysate remains at the bottom of each 2 mL tube.

steps.title: Seal filter capsules
steps.instruction: Ensure all filter capsules are properly labeled and closed on both top and bottom.

steps.title: Second incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes again at 56 °C for 3 hours.

steps.title: Evacuate lysate with syringe
steps.instruction: Using a new 3 mL–10 mL Luer‑lock syringe for each sample, hold the filter vertically, attach the syringe to the bottom cap, unscrew the top cap, and suction the lysate out of the capsule.

steps.title: Label new 2 mL tubes
steps.instruction: Label a fresh 2 mL tube for each sample (including control) to receive downstream reagents.

steps.title: Add AW1 to Wash Plate 1
steps.instruction: Pipette 650 µL AW1 buffer into each well of Wash Plate 1 (S‑Block).

steps.title: Add AW1 to Wash Plate 2
steps.instruction: Pipette 500 µL AW1 buffer into each well of Wash Plate 2 (S‑Block).

steps.title: Prepare bind plates
steps.instruction: Set up bind plates (each holds up to 300 µL lysate); prepare as many plates as needed based on lysate volume.

steps.title: Add AW2 to Wash Plate 3
steps.instruction: Pipette 500 µL AW2 buffer into each well of Wash Plate 3 (S‑Block).

steps.title: Add AW2 to Wash Plate 4
steps.instruction: Pipette 500 µL AW2 buffer into each well of Wash Plate 4 (S‑Block).

steps.title: Add water‑Tween to Wash Plate 5
steps.instruction: Pipette 500 µL RNase‑free water containing Tween 20 (final 0.02 %) into each well of Wash Plate 5 (Microplate).

steps.title: Add AL buffer and isopropanol
steps.instruction: To each well of every bind plate, add 300 µL AL buffer followed by 300 µL isopropanol.

steps.title: Add magnetic particles to first bind plate
steps.instruction: Vortex the MagAttract magnetic particle bottle briefly, then add 30 µL particles to each well of the first bind plate.

steps.title: Add lysate to bind plates
steps.instruction: Dispense 200 µL lysate into each bind plate well; if lysate volume is insufficient, supplement with TES buffer (or DNeasy lysis buffer) to reach 200 µL.

steps.title: Run DNA uptake program
steps.instruction: Place a new rod cover into the first bind plate and start the BioSprint ‘DNA uptake’ program, selecting the appropriate number of bind plates (2–7). At program end, DNA and the rod cover reside in the last bind plate.

steps.title: Run eDNA extract program
steps.instruction: Using the last bind plate (containing DNA and rod cover) together with the other reagent plates, start the BioSprint ‘eDNA extract’ program.

steps.title: Transfer eluates to tubes
steps.instruction: Pipette the processed extracts from the elution plate into labeled Eppendorf tubes.

steps.title: Dispose of BioSprint waste
steps.instruction: Place all toxic BioSprint waste into the designated hazardous waste container.

steps.title: Wash plates with bleach
steps.instruction: Wash all blocks and plates repeatedly with water, then incubate them in a bleach‑water bath for 1 day.

steps.title: Dishwasher cleaning
steps.instruction: After the bleach bath, run the blocks and plates through a dishwasher for reuse.

steps.title: Add elution buffer
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µL TE buffer or AE buffer into each well of the elution plate (Microplate).
